chat.text: Draw a system architecture diagram of a web application: a client/browser, a load balancer, three application servers, a database, and a Redis cache. Connect them with labeled arrows showing the request flow.

I'll create a clean left-to-right architecture diagram: client, load balancer, three app servers in a vertical stack, then database/cache on the right. I'll use shared arrow labels sparingly to avoid clutter.

This diagram shows the request path through a typical web app: the browser sends an HTTP request to the load balancer, which forwards traffic to one of three application servers. Each app server can query the database for persistent data and Redis for cached data, then the response travels back through the same route to the client.
